title: Pizza with meat (not pepperoni), school lunch, thick crust

content.title: About
content.content: A meat pizza that differs from classic pepperoni is often served in school cafeterias as a hearty lunch. The dough has a thick crust (3417), making it denser and more filling. The meat topping can be beef, chicken, or ham, combined with tomato sauce, cheese, and vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A thick crust retains more moisture, keeping the toppings juicy.
In school menus pizza is considered a source of protein and carbohydrates for active children.
Meat used in school pizzas undergoes strict quality and sanitary checks.
Pizza is typically prepared in large batches in schools, ensuring consistent taste and texture.
A "chicken and vegetable pizza" variant is often offered as a lower‑calorie option.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides a complete set of amino acids essential for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese supplies calcium, supporting bone and tooth health in children.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomatoes and meat contain vitamins B6 and B12, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Dietary fiber from vegetables
items.content: Added vegetables (bell pepper, onion) increase fiber content, aiding digestion.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: The combination of carbs from the crust and protein from the meat provides sustained satiety.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Thick crust and cheese make the pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially for less active children.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt in the sauce and cheese can raise sodium intake, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Cheese and certain meats may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: If margarine is used instead of olive oil, trans fats may be present.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pizza into serving pieces and eat it while hot. Fresh vegetables or herbs can be added for extra nutrition. For a crisp crust, reheat briefly in an oven or grill rather than a microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness. Discard if it develops an off‑smell or taste.
